10042499:
Testimony of Garrett Mason in Opposition to LD 1005
An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler Plan Reviews
Good Morning, Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety. My name is Garrett Mason. I am a resident of Lisbon Falls and a Partner at Dirigo Public Affairs. I am here today speaking on behalf of my client, the Associated Builders and Contractors of Maine, a trade association advocating for contractors, builders, and industry professionals statewide. Our members rely on clear, consistent regulations to deliver safe, high-quality projects, and that's why we oppose LD 1005
Maine's current system delivers a uniform standard for sprinkler installations. This single, statewide approach ensures all projects follow NFPA and MUBEC codes consistently, giving contractors clear rules to work by. It's a system that's proven efficient and consistent.
Handing control to municipalities would break this uniformity. Each town could interpret codes differently, set its own rules, and create a patchwork of conflicting standards. That's not just a headache for contractors--it could weaken safety and raise costs as builders try to meet local demands.
The state already offers preliminary permits for $50, issued instantly online, letting work start right away. Full permits follow in 1 day to 3 weeks, depending on project size.
We believe the system works fine as is and there is no need to change it. We urge you to vote "Ought Not to Pass" on LD 1005.

Testimony of Representative Grayson Lookner presenting
LD 1005, An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler Plan Reviews
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety

Good morning, Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and honorable colleagues on the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety. My name is Grayson Lookner, and I represent House District 113, which includes several neighborhoods in Portland. I'm here today to present LD 1005, An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler Plan Reviews.

This is a simple bill which would let trained municipal fire departments review sprinkler plans instead of relying solely on the state. This is a practical fix for a real problem--right now, the backlog at the state level slows down housing projects, especially in busy towns where every delay adds cost and frustration.

The bill makes sure this isn't a trade-off on safety. Only towns with fire departments that have National Fire Protection Association (NFPA)-certified staff and a clear review process can take this on. That means plans still get checked thoroughly against all codes, just by people who know the local buildings and needs.

For towns with the capacity, this is a no-brainer. It'll get permits moving faster, take pressure off the state, and keep safety tight. I hope the committee will pass LD 1005 quickly--it's a small change that'll make a difference for housing and common sense.

Thank you, I'd be happy to answer any questions.

District 113: Part of Portland

Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler Plan Reviews To the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety

Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and honorable members of the Criminal Justice and Public Safety Committee,
My name is Representative Holly Eaton, and I proudly represent House District 15, which includes the island and coastal communities of Deer Isle, Stonington, Brooklin, Tremont, Southwest Harbor, Frenchboro, Swan's Island, Isle au Haut, and Vinalhaven.
This bill proposes a simple, commonsense change: allowing municipal re departments with personnel certi ed by the National Fire Protection Association to conduct sprinkler system plan reviews. I believe this change will be especially impactful for small and rural towns across Maine, and particularly the unbridged islands I represent.
In rural areas like mine, projects that require sprinkler system approval often face delays and additional costs simply because reviews must go through third-party providers or state agencies that are far removed from the community. By empowering quali ed local re departments to conduct these reviews, we can make the process more ef cient, more cost-effective, and more responsive to the needs of the people on the ground.
This is about trusting trained professionals who already serve their communities with distinction --and who often know the buildings, landscapes, and infrastructure better than anyone else--to play a greater role in ensuring safety. It's also about equity--making sure rural towns and island communities aren't at a disadvantage simply because of their geography.

10042008:
Paul Tardif Eastern Fire LD 1005
HP 652, LD 1005 April 7, 2025 09:30 am Criminal Justice & Public Safety Joint Committee
An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler Plan Reviews
Good Morning, my name is Paul Tardif, I have been in the fire sprinkler industry since 1973, and have worked on sprinkler projects in 15 states, as well in Maine for 36 years; I can speak with experience regarding how the state of Maine is ahead of most states in efficiency, quality and consistency.
The only complaints regarding review and permitting at the state level (that I am aware of) was during a recent transition when the state sprinkler reviewer for the last ten years retired; that slowed things down for a few months. At this time plan review & permitting is normally completed in less than two weeks, never more than three and often in 2 to 3 days.
The main point offered in getting this bill sponsored was the impact that permitting delays created for the construction industry. I do know that many subcontractors including sprinkler subcontractors tell builders and owners that they can't start a project because they are waiting on state permits, when in fact they are too backlogged and simply aren't able to meet the schedule. This also speaks to the shortage of personnel in Maine's fire sprinkler industry.
The fact that any Maine licensed, qualified fire sprinkler contractor can obtain a temporary permit immediately for any project alleviates all the concerns that the LD 1005 intends to rectify.
The Maine Fire Sprinkler Association got together in the late 1980s to help create and fund positions in the State Fire Marshal's Office to regulate the industry, provide consistent code interpretations and thorough plan review. That system has served Maine well for 37 years; the model is significantly more efficient than in most other states.
We urge the committee to not move LD 1005 forward, doing so would not be an improvement but would result in increased costs, delays and inconsistencies.
Thank you for you consideration ~ Paul Tardif VP/ Pre-Construction Manager / Eastern Fire

Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Support For
LD 1005 --An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler

April 7, 2025
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and distinguished members of the Criminal
Justice and Public Safety Committee, my name is Rebecca Graham, and I am testifying in support for LD 1005, at the direction of MMA's Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). Our LPC is made up of individuals
from across Maine with municipal officials elected by their peers across Maine's 35 Senate districts representing communities with very different access to available enforcement resources and local
capacity.
When reviewing this proposed bill, municipal officials expressed a desire to adequately staff the
Office of the State Fire Marshal to conduct the reviews necessary for backlogged permits and while some communities have delegated review authority for some entities, the vast majority are reliant on the office. The backlog is significant and has hindered economic development in some areas of the state; One
community shared that their proximity to New Hampshire led to losing one significant economic
development project to the state because of this backlog within the office.
The lack of adequate investment in the state systems that are intended to suppoit local processes
continues to be a hinderance to local development across the board but the reasons for the review remain
important.
However, there was also recognition that splitting out just one element of the necessaiy reviews conducted by the fire marshal's office will be unlikely to relieve the backlog and may result in further
delays because a developer will still be required to have different plan elements reviewed with the office.
Where there is local capacity, officials welcome delegated authority but it's important to note that there are only a limited number of communities that may have this capacity locally.
Officials support mechanisms that allow municipalities to be part of the solution instead of the ones that simply devalue the regulatory need and seek to remove it. For these reasons, officials support the policy theory behind this bill but also recognize it will only apply to a narrow set of development proposals, and likely can be achieved through delegated authority processes already with limited local capacity to take up the charge.

LD 1005 - An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct

Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and honorable members of the Criminal Justice and
Public Safety Committee, my name is Shawn Esler, and it is a privilege to serve as the State Fire Marshal.
I write neither for nor against LD 1005.
In 2024 alone, the Office of State Fire Marshal (FMO) Plan Review Division consisting of four personnel reviewed 886 construction projects valued at $1.9 Billion across Maine. Additionally, our Office
reviewed 786 sprinkler projects, and issued 192 fire sprinkler contractor, inspector, and RMS licenses.
Currently Title 25 �2448-A allows for a municipality to conduct municipal reviews of development, however, the law does not allow for a municipality to conduct sprinkler reviews.
At times, our construction permit process has been delayed. This is a symptom of a relatively small number of staff serving an entire State. Since 2018, the value of annual projects being reviewed has climbed over $1 Billion demonstrating the workload has nearly doubled in the last few years. Addressing
concerns related to workload imbalance and delays is a priority of mine.
However, regarding sprinklers, our office issues preliminary approval immediately upon receipt of
application and payment. I have enclosed a copy of that approval for your review at the bottom of my
testimony. This preliminary approval allows a contractor to begin construction immediately, ensuring that
a project can move forward without delay. The FMO issues these approvals based on our pre-established relationship via contractor licensing. The FMO then conducts a full review, ensuring the project meets fire code, MUBBC, and engineering requirements. A sprinkler permit is then issued after a full set of
plans have been submitted. Since 2018, sprinkler permits issuance has soared from 500 permits annually to 786 in 2024, a 57.2 percent increase in workjust in this area alone.
LD 1005 aims to allow a municipality to conduct sprinkler reviews after registering with the
Commissioner of Public Safety. Before enacting this law, I ask you to consider the following points:
0 Experience- The FMO has been the sole point of conducting sprinkler reviews for decades.
0 Education- The FMO Plan Reviewers are Certified Fire Inspectors, Certified Plan Reviewers,
and receive hundreds of hours of specialized training specific to sprinkler plan review at the National Fire Academy. Over half of our Plans Review staff have also worked in the sprinkler industry, gaining valuable experience. Lastly, our Plans Review Supervisor is a certified Fire Protection Specialist and Licensed Plumber, ensuring all projects comply with code.
v C0ntinuity- The FMO provides uniform and consistent guidance enacted by Legislature across
the State eliminating disparity between communities.

April 4, 2025
To: Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety From: Steve Sloan, Fire Chief
RE: Maine LD 1005 "An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Fire Sprinkler Plans Review"
Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and esteemed members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety:
My name is Steve Sloan, and I am writing today to express my strong support for LD 1005, An Act to Allow Municipal Fire Departments with Trained Personnel to Conduct Sprinkler Plan Reviews.
This legislation represents a common-sense approach to increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of the plan review process in Maine. By allowing municipal fire departments--when they have qualified, trained personnel--to conduct sprinkler plan reviews, we can significantly streamline the construction permitting process, while maintaining safety and compliance with all relevant standards.
First and foremost, LD 1005 would improve operational efficiency. Many local fire departments already have personnel who are highly trained and certified in fire protection systems and codes. Enabling them to perform these reviews locally reduces redundancy and makes use of existing expertise within the community.
Second, this bill would help reduce potential delays in the permitting and construction process. Under the current system, sprinkler plan reviews may be subject to backlogs at the state level due capacity limitations or unforeseen delays. This can lead to unnecessary waiting periods for developers, contractors, and property owners. Allowing municipalities to take on this responsibility, when they are equipped to do so, will alleviate pressure on centralized resources and allow for faster processing.
Third, municipal fire departments are uniquely positioned to ensure that sprinkler plans conform to local codes and ordinances. Local officials are intimately familiar with the specific fire safety needs, zoning requirements, and building characteristics of their communities. Their input during the plan review process helps ensure that projects meet not only state requirements but also the specific needs of the municipality, improving public safety outcomes.
Finally, this bill supports faster turnaround times for permit issuance, which directly reduces total construction timelines. In today's economic climate, where time is money, any improvement in

processing speed can make a meaningful difference. This legislation will help accelerate project completion and occupancy, encouraging growth and investment across Maine communities. LD 1005 empowers local authorities, promotes public safety, and supports the needs of the construction and development sectors. I urge the committee to support this bill and allow qualified municipal fire departments to contribute more directly to this important aspect of community safety and development. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely,
Steve Sloan Fire Chief, City of Westbrook, Maine
